questions.q: Let $a > 0, a \ne 1$. Then, the set $S$ of all positive real numbers $b$ satisfying~$\left(1 + a^{2}\right)\left(1 + b^{2}\right) = 4ab$ is
options: a finite set containing more than one element
questions.solution:
Given relation&

$\left(1 + a^{2}\right)\left(1 + b^{2}\right) = 4ab$

$⇒ a^{2} + b^{2} - 2ab = 2ab - 1 - a^{2}b^{2}$

$⇒ \left(a - b\right)2 = - \left(1 - ab\right)2$

$∵ a > 0, a \ne 1$ and b is a positive real number~

$∴ \left(a - b\right)2 \ne 0 \ne - \left(1 - ab\right)2$, because $\left(a - b\right)2$
and $\left(1 - ab\right)2$ are non-negative real numbers.~

$∴$ Set $S$ is an empty set.

questions.q: The number of ordered pairs $\left(a, b\right)$ of positive integers such that $\dfrac{2a - 1}{b} and \dfrac{2b - 1}{a}$ are both integers is&
questions.solution:
For positive integers '$a$' and '$b$' the numbers $\dfrac{2a - 1}{b} and \dfrac{2b - 1}{a}$ are integers if '$a$' and '$b$' and odd integers because '$2a - 1$' and '$2b - 1$' are odd integers. 

Now, let $\dfrac{2a - 1}{b} = \alpha$ and $\dfrac{2b - 1}{a} = \beta$, where $\alpha, \beta$ are integers.

then $2a - 1 = \alphab$ and $2b - 1 = \betaa$

so $4a - 2 = \alpha \left(\betaa + 1\right)

$⇒ a = $\dfrac{\alpha + 2}{4 - \alpha\beta}

$∵$ $a$ is an integer, then $0 < \alpha\beta < 4$

$∴$ Possible value of $\alpha = 1, 2 or 3 and \beta = 1, 2 or 3$

such that $0 < \alpha\beta < 4$

Now, when \left(\alpha, \beta\right) = \left(1, 1\right), then \left(a, b\right) = \left(1, 1\right)

When \left(\alpha, \beta\right) = \left(1, 2\right), then \left(a, b\right) have no value

When $( \alpha, \beta ) = ( 1, 3 )$, then \left(a, b\right)$ = $\left(3, 5\right)$ and similarly when $\left(\alpha, \beta\right)$ = $\left(3, 1\right)$, then $\left(a, b\right)$ = $\left(5, 3\right)$ 

So, number of ordered pairs $\left(a, b\right)$ is $3$.

questions.q:
Let $N$ be the set of positive integers. For all $n \in \mathbb{N},$ let ${f}_{n} = \left(n + 1\right)^{1} / 3 - n^{1 / 3}$ and $A = \left\{n \in \mathbb{N}: {f}_{n + 1} < \dfrac{1}{3\left(n + 1\right)^{2} / 3} < {f}_{n}\right\}$
Then,
options: the complement of $A$ in $N$ is nonempty, but finite
$A$ and its complement in $N$ are both infinite
questions.solution:
It is given that for& $n \in N$

${f}_{n} = \left(n + 1\right)1 / 3 - n^{1 / 3}$

$= \dfrac{\left(n + 1\right) - n}{\left(n + 1\right)2 / 3 + \left(n + 1\right)2 / 3n^{2 / 3} + n^{2 / 3}}$

$= \dfrac{1}{\left(n + 1\right)2 / 3 + \left(n + 1\right)2 / 3n^{2 / 3} + n^{2 / 3}}$

$∵ ∀ n \in N$

$3n^{2 / 3} < \left(n + 1\right)2 / 3 + \left(n + 1\right)2 / 3n^{2 / 3} + n^{2 / 3} < 3\left(n + 1\right)2 / 3$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{3\left(n + 1\right)2 / 3} < \dfrac{1}{+ \left(n + 1\right)2 / 3 + \left(n + 1\right)2 / 3n^{2 / 3} + n^{2 / 3}} < \dfrac{1}{3n^{2 / 3}}$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{3\left(n + 1\right)2 / 3} < {f}_{n} < \dfrac{1}{3n^{2 / 3}}$

Similarly,

$\dfrac{1}{3\left(n + 2\right)2 / 3} < {f}_{n + 1} < \dfrac{1}{3\left(n + 1\right)2 / 3}$

$∴ {f}_{n + 1} < \dfrac{1}{3\left(n + 1\right)2 / 3} < {f}_{n}, ∀ n \in N$

So, set $A = N$

questions.q: In a cinema hall, the charge per person is Rs. 200. On the first day, only $60 \%$ of the seats were filled. The owner decided to reduce the price by $20 \%$ and there was in increase of $50 \%$ in the number of spectators on the next day. The percentage increase in the revenue on the second day was
questions.solution:
Let total seats $=100$
on first day,
Ticket price $=200=\frac{60}{100} \times 100=60\therefore$ Revenue $=60 \times 200\mathrm{R}_{1}=12000$
On second day
Tricked price $=200-20 \%$ of 200
$=200-\frac{20}{100} \times 200=200-40=160$
Scents full $60+50 \%$ of 60
$=60+\frac{50}{100} \times 60\begin{array}{l}
=\begin{aligned}
60+30=90 \\
\text{ Revenue }=160 \times 90 \\
\mathrm{R}_{2}=14400 \\
\% & \text{ Increase is Revenue }=\frac{R_{2}-R_{1}}{R_{1}} \times 100 \\
&=\frac{14400-12000}{12000} \times 100 \\
&=\frac{2400}{1200} \times 100 \\
=& 20 \%
\end{aligned}
\end{array}$
